newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian government closes Abidjan student hostels.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian government closes Abidjan student hostels.

text.p: Ivory Coast's government has closed down student hostels in the commercial capital Abidjan, after a wave of unrest in the West African nation's universities.
A cabinet statement, published in the government newspaper Fraternite Matin on Saturday, accused student activists of vandalism and violence and disrupting university life there.

"In this climate of hate and insecurity, which has already led to two deaths and several injuries, it is necessary and urgent to take vigourous measures to preserve social peace in the campuses and avoid a spiral of violence," it said.

Ivory Coast's banned student union FESCI has called a series of strikes and stoppages this year to protest about grants and study and living conditions. Campuses around the country have been disrupted, closing for varying periods.
FESCI General-Secretary Guillaume Soro told the opposition Ivorian Popular Front newspaper La Voie the government order was an admission of defeat and would only make students angrier.
"We think that the authorities want to declare the academic year null and void," he said.

The government statement said that the closure of the halls of residence, announced on Friday, was designed to stop students who wanted to continue studying becoming the victims of threats and attacks from student militants based in the hostels.
Soro rejected the charge that FESCI militants were behind the attacks.
